body: [{"streamId":"01a0de10-e8dc-7404-a168-70c0b2fcc123","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Tasks.Events.TaskAdded","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a0de10-e8dc-7404-a168-70c0b2fcc123\u0022,\u0022ProjectId\u0022:\u002201a0a27f-abdf-7731-84aa-d604e9bc53ca\u0022,\u0022Objective\u0022:\u0022A walked detail page whose title names the hybrid model (\\u00272023 Toyota Corolla Hybrid\\u0027) is saved as that model even when the extraction splits it into a base model plus trim, so real Corolla Hybrids and Camry Hybrids stop being dropped as the wrong model\u0022,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[\u0022The extraction prompt (src/Odonomics/Extraction/prompt.md) and the schema\\u0027s model and trim descriptions state the rule explicitly: model is the full model name as the page\\u0027s own title prints it, keeping a variant word such as Hybrid, Prime, or Plug-in as part of the model, never moved into trim; trim is the grade alone (LE, SE, XLE, Limited); with the worked example \\u0027Toyota Corolla Hybrid / LE Sedan 4D\\u0027 yielding model \\u0027Corolla Hybrid\\u0027 and trim \\u0027LE\\u0027; the prompt\\u0027s existing injection guard and null rules are unchanged\u0022,\u0022As a deterministic backstop, the walk accepts a detail page whose extracted make and base model match the query but whose model and trim lack the word Hybrid when the page text\\u0027s own title line reads \\u0027\\u003Cyear\\u003E \\u003Cmake\\u003E \\u003Cbase model\\u003E Hybrid\\u0027 (a single title pattern anchored on the year, make, and base model, so a gas Corolla page that merely mentions a Corolla Hybrid elsewhere is still rejected); the saved candidate\\u0027s model is the query\\u0027s model; the per-pair line and drop reasons are unchanged for a page that fails both checks; proven by tests over fixtures cut from the recorded pages detail-3.txt and detail-7.txt (accepted) and an existing gas-Corolla fixture (still rejected)\u0022,\u0022ListingQuery.MatchesExtractedVehicle keeps its current signature and behavior for the API sources; the page-text check lives beside it (a new method or a walk-side helper) and is called only from the walk; the README\\u0027s walk section says a hybrid named in the page title counts as a match; dotnet build and dotnet test succeed with zero warnings; commits are small with conventional messages, no em dashes, no AI attribution\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Bugfix\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022Reported by run session odonomics-59 on 2026-09-26 during walk run 5 on main 17ebf27 (notes/run-session-2026-09-22.md, Gaps found), verified by the orchestrator: ~/Library/Application Support/Odonomics/walks/carvana/20260926-121057/corolla-hybrid/detail-3.txt and detail-7.txt are titled \\u00272023 Toyota Corolla Hybrid\\u0027 and \\u00272020 Toyota Corolla Hybrid\\u0027, describe the car as the Corolla Hybrid LE, and list the engine as \\u00274-Cyl, Hybrid, 1.8 Liter\\u0027; the walk dropped both as \\u0027wrong model (doesn\\u0027t match Toyota Corolla Hybrid: 2023 Toyota Corolla LE)\\u0027. Run 4 had the identical drop on this pair (detail 8) and three wrong-model drops on carvana / Camry Hybrid, so it recurs and costs a real candidate plus a cap slot each time. Code: extraction runs through the claude CLI with src/Odonomics/Extraction/prompt.md and schema.json (schema already says \\u0027e.g. Insight, Corolla Hybrid, Camry Hybrid, Prius\\u0027 for model, which the model ignores when the page prints \\u0027Corolla Hybrid / LE Sedan 4D\\u0027), returning ExtractionClient\\u0027s record with Model and Trim; WalkCommand.cs line 256 calls query.MatchesExtractedVehicle(make, model, trim, year) and line 258 GasOnlyBeforeHybridYear for the reason text; src/Odonomics/Sources/ListingQuery.cs lines 17 to 59 hold IsHybridVariant, BaseModelName, MatchesMakeAndBaseModel, ContainsHybridText, and the matcher. The page text is in scope at the call site (it is what was extracted from). Existing walk fixtures live under tests/Odonomics.Tests/fixtures/walks; extraction tests are tests/Odonomics.Tests/Extraction/ExtractionGroundingTests.cs. Prefer the deterministic title check as the guarantee and the prompt wording as the improvement; a unit test cannot exercise the model. Do not touch the run skill file in the project home; the orchestrator updates
